## Overview

RLMADJ04 is a confirmed-input wider-outcome companion in #409 D1. It asks **which wave-1 skills go with more subsequent receptive-grammar gain** in the Byrne cohort. TROG receptive grammar at wave 3 is conditioned on its own wave-1 baseline and the mutually adjusted, standardised wave-1 levels of BAS word reading (`basread`), BPVS receptive vocabulary (`bpvs`), verbal memory (`basdig`), verbal reasoning (`bassim`) and age. All five measurement inputs have confirmed instrument identities and ceilings.

_Adjusted associations only._ The Byrne cohort has no intervention: every coefficient is a between-child conditional association (`causal_status="none"`), not an effect of changing the predictor. Own-baseline adjustment makes this a post-score-given-baseline model rather than a literal difference-score regression. The group dummies absorb observational cohort composition and are nuisance terms, not interpretable group effects.

_Frame and exclusions._ The complete-case frame contains 69 of the prepared extract's 97 children: 21 with Down syndrome, 30 average readers and 18 reading-matched children. Twenty-eight children lack at least one required outcome or predictor value. No predictor is imputed. The analysis therefore assumes that complete-case selection has not materially distorted these conditional associations.

_Reading-matched selection._ The reading-matched group was selected on BAS word-reading level, which is a focal predictor here. Pooling that group can distort the word-reading slope and coefficients conditional on it, even after nuisance group adjustment. This companion is useful for descriptive triangulation, but it is not a selection-free estimate and must be read alongside group-specific descriptive evidence.

## Model

For child $i$ with wave-1 TROG logit $b_i$ and standardised wave-1 predictors $z_{k,i}$:

$$
y_i \sim \mathrm{BetaBinomial}(20,\ p_i,\ \kappa),
\qquad
\operatorname{logit}(p_i) = \alpha + \gamma_{\text{own}} b_i +
\textstyle\sum_k \beta_k z_{k,i} + \boldsymbol{\beta}_{\text{grp}}^{\top}
\mathbf{d}_i ,
$$

where $y_i$ is the wave-3 TROG receptive-grammar count (confirmed ceiling 20), $\beta_k \sim \mathrm{Normal}(0, 0.3)$ are the mutually adjusted per-SD slopes, and $\mathbf{d}_i$ are the group-nuisance dummies (reference: average readers, the largest fitted group). The bivariate comparison refits each predictor alone while retaining the own baseline and nuisance structure, and the prior-sensitivity sweep varies the slope sigma from 0.3 to 0.5 and 0.7 and widens the own-baseline coupling prior $\gamma_{\text{own}} \sim \mathrm{Normal}(1, 0.25)$ to SD 0.5. The Beta-Binomial concentration takes the dispersion-scale prior of the Byrne historical families, $1/\sqrt{\kappa} \sim \mathrm{HalfNormal}(0.25)$: at this 20-block denominator a HalfNormal on the concentration itself gave the near-Binomial limit essentially no prior mass and held the fitted concentration against it (2026-08-22 adjusted-family review).
